candidate: AGENTS.md as the canonical instruction file with a one-line @AGENTS.md import in CLAUDE.md (AGENTS.md format undated; Claude Code 2.1.277+)
what: Put the kit's rules block in AGENTS.md, which Codex and Cursor read natively, and make CLAUDE.md import it so that Claude Code reads the same text once.
problem_here: install.py writes the block to CLAUDE.md and creates that file when it is missing (lines 212-222). In a repository that has only AGENTS.md this makes Claude Code 2.1.277+ stop reading the user's AGENTS.md. Codex and Cursor never see the block at all.
mechanism: Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only when no CLAUDE.md exists, unless CLAUDE.md imports it; the import is the documented shared-file pattern and the file is not loaded twice.
evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog (2.1.277, 2026-09-18), vendor docs read 2026-11-11; https://agents.md/ ; a census of 22,854 repositories found that CLAUDE.md usually points to AGENTS.md where both exist (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31715 v2, 2026-10-26, measured by the paper's authors). The regression is inferred from the docs plus a local read of install.py and was not run.
maturity: AGENTS.md format: repository agentsmd/agents.md last pushed 2026-09-10, stewarded by the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation, licence and first release not checked; read by Codex, Cursor and others per its site. Claude Code support first released 2026-09-18 (2.1.277), fixed for telemetry-off sessions in 2.1.281.
cost: One installer change plus a migration that moves the existing block. Failure modes: a user setting of managed-only ignores project files; Codex stops reading at 32 KiB; nested AGENTS.md files sit closer to the code than the root file. Attack surface: one more file to protect.
simpler_alternative: Write the same block into both files (duplicates text and drifts).
reason: Needed for both ports and fixes a regression the current installer can cause today, for a few lines of code.
cheap_local_trial: About 10 minutes: in a scratch repository with AGENTS.md only, ask Claude Code to repeat a marker line from it; add an empty CLAUDE.md and repeat (the marker should vanish); put @AGENTS.md in CLAUDE.md and repeat (the marker returns once).

candidate: Agent Skills spec conformance plus a byte-identical skill copy in .agents/skills (specification page undated, no version shown)
what: Keep the nn-training skill inside the open SKILL.md limits and install the same bytes into .agents/skills for Codex and Cursor.
problem_here: The skill exists only under .claude/skills. Codex does not read that folder; Cursor reads it only through a compatibility path.
mechanism: Codex and Cursor both load .agents/skills. The name must equal the folder name, the description is at most 1024 characters and SKILL.md stays under 500 lines. Native Windows has no symlinks, so the copy is a real copy checked by hash.
evidence: https://agentskills.io/specification ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills ; https://cursor.com/docs/skills (spec and vendor docs, read 2026-11-11). Benefit of curated skills: +16.6 points in SkillsBench (https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12670 v4, 2026-06-14, measured by its authors on non-training tasks).
maturity: Open format that began at Anthropic; first release and licence of the spec not checked; SKILL.md-style skills appear in 9 of 11 harnesses in a source-code study (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00006 v1, 2026-07-15).
cost: A second copy to keep in step; Cursor then sees two copies (see the conflict-check candidate). No money and no network.
simpler_alternative: Rely on Cursor's compatibility loading of .claude/skills and give Codex no skill (Codex then has no procedure).
reason: Required for the Codex port, and the format is the one thing all three agents share.
cheap_local_trial: About 15 minutes: copy the skill folder to .agents/skills/nn-training in a scratch repository, start Codex and Cursor, ask each to list its skills and confirm the name appears once per agent.

candidate: One guard policy core with thin per-agent hook adapters (Claude Code 2.1.322; Codex hooks docs undated; Cursor hooks.json version 1)
what: Keep the decision rules in one stdlib module and add a small adapter per agent that reads that agent's hook payload and writes that agent's answer format.
problem_here: nn_guard.py reads Claude Code tool names and fields only, and most of its rules answer 'ask'. Codex PreToolUse has no 'ask'; Cursor preToolUse does not enforce 'ask'; both let the tool run when the hook fails; Codex edits arrive as a patch with no file_path; Cursor may run Claude Code hooks as well as its own.
mechanism: The adapter maps tool names and inputs to a common shape, maps 'ask' to 'deny' where the agent or the mode cannot ask, sets failClosed on Cursor, wraps the Codex command so that any non-zero exit becomes exit 2, extracts paths from patch bodies and drops a second call with the same tool-use id.
evidence: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks and https://cursor.com/docs/agent/hooks (vendor docs, undated, read 2026-11-11). Open-source guards already use the layout: cc-safety-net v2.7.9 covers 16 CLIs and stop-that-shit v0.2.5 documents a host adapter contract. No independent measurement of any adapter was found.
maturity: Codex and Cursor hooks are documented and on by default; the pages carry no version. The adapter layout is used by several small guards (weak adoption signal).
cost: Roughly 100 lines per adapter plus tests, re-tested per agent release. Failure modes: undocumented headless behaviour, unknown apply_patch input shape, a Codex hook timeout still lets the tool run. Attack surface: two more hook config files the agent could edit.
simpler_alternative: Copy nn_guard.py and rename fields (the 'ask' rules would then be silently unenforced).
reason: Without the mapping the ported guard looks installed and enforces almost nothing; this is the main port risk found.
cheap_local_trial: About 20 minutes: register a 20-line hook that dumps stdin to a file in Codex and in Cursor, run one shell command, one file edit and one file read, and compare the payloads with the fields nn_guard.py expects.

candidate: Guard-liveness canary in selftest and before each unattended loop (own proposal derived from the hook docs; no version)
what: A harmless command that the guard must deny; if it executes, it writes a marker saying the guard is not live.
problem_here: Codex does not run new or changed hooks until a person trusts them again, and Codex and default Cursor let the tool run when a hook fails. After a kit upgrade or with a broken interpreter the guard can be off with no visible sign.
mechanism: The loop driver asks the agent to run the canary with a fresh nonce and proceeds only when the guard log holds a denial with that nonce and the marker file is absent; the check repeats every K runs.
evidence: Motivation: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks (trust by hash, tool may run on hook error) and https://cursor.com/docs/agent/hooks (failClosed off by default), read 2026-11-11. The canary is my proposal; nobody has measured it.
maturity: Not an existing product; a new check inside the kit.
cost: About 40 lines and one agent turn per check. Failure mode: an agent that declines to run the canary stalls the preflight, which must count as not verified.
simpler_alternative: Tell users in the docs to re-trust hooks after every upgrade (advice, not enforced).
reason: Turns two silent fail-open paths into a hard stop before unattended work starts.
cheap_local_trial: About 10 minutes on the current kit: disable the hook in settings, ask the agent to run a marker-writing command and confirm the marker appears; re-enable the hook and confirm a logged denial instead.

candidate: Effect-bound launch approval: hashes of frozen paths and config in the run manifest, verified by harness code after the run (idea from arXiv 2609.28586 v1)
what: Record what a run may change, then check what it did change, instead of trusting the approved command line.
problem_here: The guard judges the text of a tool call. A training script it allowed can edit the evaluator, read sealed data or change config by indirect means; the README already calls the guard a seatbelt and not a sandbox.
mechanism: expctl launch writes hashes of frozen_paths and the config and a listing of sealed paths into the manifest. After the run the harness recomputes them; any difference, or any check it cannot complete, marks the run invalid and not keepable.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28586 v1 (2026-09-23), measured by its authors: no invocation-only record suffices; with effect-bound records residual unapproved effects fell from 10 to 3 on 17 holdout workflows (macro recall 0.926, precision 0.941). Small holdout; software workflows, not training.
maturity: Preprint with a Claude Code hook integration (code and licence not inspected). The kit already has expctl hash and a manifest schema to extend.
cost: Hashing time per run and new manifest fields. It does not detect reads of sealed data without operating-system support. No money and no network.
simpler_alternative: Run the final evaluation from a clean copy of the evaluator only (covers the evaluator, not config or data).
reason: Protects the frozen evaluator in the unattended loop, where nobody reviews each command; a trial is needed to size false alarms.
cheap_local_trial: About 20 minutes: a fake CPU run whose script edits a frozen file through an imported helper; confirm that the guard allows the launch and that a post-run hash comparison flags the run.

candidate: Skill conflict and duplicate-copy check in installer and selftest (from arXiv 2610.11647 v2)
what: List every installed skill whose name or description overlaps the kit's skill, and verify that all kit copies are byte-identical.
problem_here: The port puts copies of the skill in .claude/skills and .agents/skills, and Cursor reads both plus .codex/skills. Users also install large skill collections.
mechanism: Hash every copy against the install manifest, compare names and description keywords across all skill folders each agent reads, and report which copy each agent loads.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11647 v2 (2026-10-13), measured by its authors on 312 confirmed pairs, 3 models and 6,368 runs: a similar skill takes over 1 run in 5 without lowering task completion; the final reply names the skill used in 0.9% of those runs; a pre-tool hook at the first skill read restores fidelity.
maturity: Preprint; no tool is needed. Cursor's multi-folder loading is documented at https://cursor.com/docs/skills (undated).
cost: A short stdlib check. Keyword overlap gives false positives, so it reports and does not block.
simpler_alternative: Install one copy only and tell users of the other agents to copy it by hand.
reason: The port itself creates the duplicate copies the paper shows to be harmful, and the failure does not show in the transcript.
cheap_local_trial: About 15 minutes: add a dummy skill with an overlapping description to a scratch repository, start the same training request five times and count which skill file is read first.

candidate: Durable hash-chained guard log written before the decision is returned (idea from CATP, arXiv 2609.38223 v1)
what: Make the audit log usable as evidence: write and flush the entry first, chain each entry to the previous one, and deny when the log cannot be written.
problem_here: audit() in nn_guard.py ignores write errors, keeps a single rotated segment so older history is overwritten, does not log allowed calls and has no integrity check. An unattended loop needs the log as its record of what was refused.
mechanism: Each entry carries the config hash and the previous entry's hash; the head hash is stored in each run manifest; a verifier walks the chain offline.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38223 v1 (2026-09-28), its authors' evaluation: 13 of 13 expected outcomes, about 85 ms median hook overhead, about 174 ms offline verification; it states that normalization collisions limit what a receipt proves. A survey finds tamper-evident traces rarely reported (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04990 v6).
maturity: Preprint targeting Claude Code and Codex; code and licence not checked. The kit change needs only stdlib hashlib.
cost: One flush per decision and a few lines. A chain detects edits but not deletion of the whole file. Denying when the disk is full can stall a loop, which is the safe side.
simpler_alternative: Keep the plain log and copy it into each run directory at launch.
reason: Cheap and useful as the unattended record, but its value depends on where the log lives relative to what the agent can write.
cheap_local_trial: About 30 minutes: add a previous-hash field in audit(), rerun the kit's guard decision tests, then edit one log line by hand and confirm a 15-line verifier reports the break.

candidate: Facts-only keep and stop gate in the loop driver (pattern in Canny and Andon; evidence from LoopArena, arXiv 2608.28281 v2)
what: Harness code decides keep, revert, continue and stop from run files and the frozen evaluator; the agent's statements only advise.
problem_here: Upgrade goal 1 requires keep or revert to be decided by harness code. An agent that both runs the experiment and decides whether it worked is exposed to every failure mode LoopArena lists.
mechanism: Each round the driver computes an evidence packet from run artifacts (metric, budget used, verification status) and applies fixed rules; the agent receives the packet and cannot overrule it.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.28281 v2 (2026-10-13), its authors' benchmark: the best strict success of a model acting as loop controller is 36.25% on 80 full tasks; named failures are stale progress note, skipped verification, wrong budget direction and premature stop. Software tasks, not training. Canny's own benchmark showed no outcome difference (author's statement in its README).
maturity: LoopArena: Apache-2.0, 154 stars, 8 commits, no release. Canny: MIT, 135 stars. Andon: MIT, 168 stars. All weak adoption signals.
cost: Driver logic inside the kit, no dependency. Failure mode: rules that are too strict stop useful exploration.
simpler_alternative: Let the agent decide and have the reviewer subagent check afterwards (still a model judging a model).
reason: Matches the brief's requirement, and the only measurement found says models are poor at exactly these decisions.
cheap_local_trial: About 30 minutes: a dry-run driver over three fake runs (better, worse, metric missing) that prints keep, revert and invalid with no agent involved.

candidate: Rule ledger with origin, enforcing check and review-by date, plus rule replay (arXiv 2610.32578 v1; Andon defect ledger)
what: A table that records for each kit rule the failure that caused it, the code that enforces it and when it was last re-tested.
problem_here: The CLAUDE.md block carries nine rules as prose, with no record of which still matter or which the guard already enforces.
mechanism: A small file that selftest checks for overdue review dates. A rule leaves the always-loaded block once code enforces it. Replay means re-running the original failure with and without the rule.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32578 v1 (2026-10-23), one repository, exploratory, measured by its authors: 48 of 118 failures traced to stale documentation; in 3 of 5 replays the failure did not recur with or without its fix; a mechanical check stopped one failure in every run while a written rule did not change behaviour. Andon's README describes a ledger with review-by dates checked by a script (no outcome data).
maturity: Preprint case study. Andon: MIT, 168 stars (weak).
cost: A table to maintain. Replays cost agent tokens and are done rarely.
simpler_alternative: A dated comment next to each rule.
reason: Keeps the instruction block short over time, which the cost measurements favour, at almost no cost.
cheap_local_trial: About 20 minutes: write the nine rules into a table and mark which have a matching guard rule; no agent needed.

candidate: Coaching deny messages that name the allowed next step (Claude Code 2.1.268 behaviour; habit-hooks claim)
what: Every guard denial says what to do instead, for example which expctl command reaches the same goal.
problem_here: When 'ask' becomes 'deny' in unattended mode the agent gets many more refusals, and a bare refusal invites a retry by another route.
mechanism: The reason text returned by the hook ends with one concrete safe action.
evidence: Claude Code 2.1.268 made built-in denials name the blocking rule and suggest a safer method (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog, read 2026-11-11). The habit-hooks README reports genuine-fix rates of 83.3% with coaching against 28.9% and 5.6% with bare messages (self-reported, not verified).
maturity: A wording practice with no dependency.
cost: Text edits in nn_guard.py; reasons are cut at 1500 characters.
simpler_alternative: Keep the current reason strings.
reason: Nearly free and in line with vendor practice, although the only measurement is self-reported.
cheap_local_trial: About 15 minutes: trigger three denials with the old and the new wording and count the agent's follow-up attempts.

candidate: Claude Code permissions.denyInsteadOfPrompting (2.1.319, 2026-11-06) and permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories (2.1.314, 2026-10-30)
what: Two settings: one denies any call that would wait on a permission prompt and lets the turn continue; the other makes the file-edit tools refuse paths outside the working directories in every permission mode.
problem_here: Unattended mode has nobody to answer prompts. Today the kit turns 'ask' into 'deny' only under bypassPermissions, which the brief does not allow outside an isolated container.
mechanism: Set both keys in the settings used for unattended runs; the guard's 'ask' answers then become denials without bypassing permissions.
evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog entries 2.1.319 and 2.1.314 (vendor changelog, read 2026-11-11). No independent test found. The same release fixed claude -p exiting 0 after its actions were refused.
maturity: 5 and 12 days old on the check date; proprietary product.
cost: Raises the minimum Claude Code version for unattended mode to 2.1.319. The interaction with the guard's own 'ask' answers is untested.
simpler_alternative: Keep mapping 'ask' to 'deny' inside the guard when a kit-level unattended flag is set.
reason: Gives no-prompt operation without bypassed approvals, but it is days old and must be tested together with the guard.
cheap_local_trial: About 10 minutes: set the first key in a scratch project, run a headless prompt that triggers an 'ask' rule and check the denial, the continued turn and the exit code.

candidate: Codex PermissionRequest hook as deny-in-code for unattended runs (Codex hooks docs, undated)
what: A Codex hook event that answers a permission request with allow or deny from code.
problem_here: Codex PreToolUse cannot answer 'ask', and in an unattended run nobody can answer a Codex approval prompt.
mechanism: Register the guard on PermissionRequest as well as PreToolUse and return deny for anything the policy would have asked about.
evidence: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks (vendor docs, read 2026-11-11). Whether hooks run under codex exec is not documented.
maturity: Documented product feature; the page shows no version or date.
cost: A small adapter addition. Unknown headless behaviour. Hooks do not cover hosted tools such as web search.
simpler_alternative: Map every 'ask' to 'deny' in the PreToolUse adapter and never rely on prompts.
reason: Possibly the cleanest no-prompt path on Codex, but its headless behaviour is unverified.
cheap_local_trial: About 20 minutes: register a logging hook on PermissionRequest, run a command that needs approval both interactively and through codex exec, and see whether the hook fires.

candidate: Two-sided step ledger in runlog (arXiv 2611.08144 v1)
what: Count the same events on both sides of a boundary, for example batches produced by the data loader and steps taken by the optimizer, and compare the counts.
problem_here: The kit watches heartbeats and curves; the paper shows that faulty runs usually finish with plausible curves and scores.
mechanism: runlog records per-epoch counters from the data side and the optimizer side; expctl compares them with each other and with the run contract.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08144 v1 (2026-11-05, workshop paper, robot reinforcement learning), measured by its authors: a curve threshold caught at most 1 in 10 faulty runs, 723 of 728 faulty runs scored within 3 standard deviations of clean runs, and the ledger caught and located every fault at about 3% extra training time. Transfer to supervised or LLM training is my inference.
maturity: Workshop preprint, one domain.
cost: A few counters in the callbacks. False alarms where counts legitimately differ (gradient accumulation, dropped last batch).
simpler_alternative: One assert on the expected number of optimizer steps per epoch.
reason: A cheap check for a failure class that curves do not show, but the evidence comes from another domain.
cheap_local_trial: About 30 minutes: a CPU toy run with a data loader that silently drops half the batches; confirm the curve looks normal and the counters disagree.

candidate: Schema-checked reviewer output with three verdicts (cloudflare/security-audit-skill pattern; no version)
what: The reviewer subagent writes a small JSON file with a verdict of confirmed, needs_validation or rejected, and harness code validates it.
problem_here: The experiment-reviewer subagent returns prose, which an unattended driver cannot act on reliably.
mechanism: A fixed schema checked by stdlib code; a missing or invalid file counts as not confirmed; the checker is never the agent that produced the result.
evidence: https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill README (read 2026-11-11). No outcome measurement. A three-valued gate is also recommended in https://www.developersdigest.tech/blog/approve-effects-not-invocations (2026-09-28, opinion).
maturity: MIT, 14 commits, last pushed 2026-06-18, about 69k stars (weak signal).
cost: A schema and a parser. Models sometimes emit invalid JSON, which the rule treats as not confirmed.
simpler_alternative: A fixed last line such as VERDICT: confirmed, read by one regular expression.
reason: The loop needs a machine-readable review result; the simpler fixed-line form may be enough.
cheap_local_trial: About 20 minutes: ask the reviewer subagent for the fixed final line on three past runs and check that a 5-line parser reads all three.

candidate: Install manifest with a SHA-256 per kit file (lockfile idea from vercel-labs/skills)
what: The installer records the hash of every file it wrote; selftest and upgrade compare against it.
problem_here: The port multiplies kit files across .claude, .agents, .codex and .cursor, an upgrade must not lose user changes, and installed copies are rarely updated.
mechanism: A JSON manifest of path and hash. Upgrade replaces only files whose hash still matches the previous manifest and reports the rest.
evidence: https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills README (read 2026-11-11): lockfile with a SHA-256 per skill and a frozen install mode. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00911 v2 (2026-07-06), measured by its authors: 53% of adopted skills are never modified after adoption.
maturity: Common packaging practice; stdlib hashlib only.
cost: About 40 lines. Line-ending conversion on Windows changes hashes unless files are written in binary mode.
simpler_alternative: A version string in each file.
reason: Needed for safe upgrades and for the duplicate-copy and guard-integrity checks.
cheap_local_trial: About 20 minutes: generate the manifest for the current install, change one hook file and confirm the comparison names it.

candidate: Paired with-kit and without-kit measurement on short-run tasks (method used by SkillsBench, arXiv 2602.12670 v4, and by the JetBrains RTK test)
what: Run the same tasks with and without the kit, several seeds each, and compare validity violations, held-out metric and total cost.
problem_here: The brief asks for a cheap, repeatable way to show that the kit helps. None exists, and two tools with strong self-reported savings measured worse when tested this way.
mechanism: A fixed task set, two arms, at least two seeds and scoring by harness code. Report kit-specific behaviours as well as outcomes, because task completion hides skill substitution.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12670 v4 (2026-06-14), its authors: the paired design showed +16.6 points for curated skills. Secondary report of the JetBrains test (https://magica.com/news/jetbrains-tests-caveman-and-rtk-token-claims, 2026-07-20): paired runs contradicted both tools' claims (primary page returned 403).
maturity: Standard experimental design.
cost: Agent tokens and GPU time for every arm and seed. Variance between agent runs is high, so small samples mislead.
simpler_alternative: Count guard denials and invalid runs from the logs of normal use (no control arm).
reason: The only credible way to know whether the kit helps; it is a method and not a component.
cheap_local_trial: About 1 hour: one 10-minute training task, two arms by two seeds, compare held-out metric, cost and rule violations.

candidate: Purpose-built training commands in expctl for evaluate, compare and budget (idea from AutoTrainess, arXiv 2606.31551 v1)
what: Give the agent dedicated commands for the steps the loop depends on instead of free-form shell.
problem_here: expctl covers launch, watch and stop. Evaluation on validation data, comparison with the baseline and budget accounting are left to ad hoc commands that the guard must then judge.
mechanism: expctl eval runs the frozen evaluator on validation data, expctl compare applies the keep rule and expctl budget reports what is left; each writes machine-readable output for the driver.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31551 v1 (2026-06-30), its authors' result on PostTrainBench: 26.94 against 23.21 for GPT-5.4 with Codex and 19.58 against 12.13 for DeepSeek-V4-Flash with OpenCode. Self-reported; no repository named. A counterweight: bash-only tooling is cheaper for bash-capable models (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20804 v1), so add few commands.
maturity: Preprint. The kit already follows this approach with expctl.
cost: More kit code to maintain; each command is a new surface to test.
simpler_alternative: Document shell recipes in the skill.
reason: The only training-specific evidence found favours interfaces over prose; add only what the loop driver needs.
cheap_local_trial: About 30 minutes: prototype a compare command on two existing runs and check that it prints keep or revert with the numbers it used.

candidate: laude-institute/harbor (version not recorded)
what: Runs coding agents on task sets inside containers and collects the results.
problem_here: A paired measurement of the kit needs repeatable isolated runs across Claude Code and Codex.
mechanism: Task definitions plus agent adapters; Docker locally or cloud sandboxes.
evidence: https://github.com/laude-institute/harbor README (read 2026-11-11). Used by SkillsBench and, per a secondary report, by the JetBrains test. No measurement of the runner itself was found.
maturity: Apache-2.0, about 6.9k stars (weak); first release and latest version not recorded.
cost: Needs Docker and a package install. GPU pass-through in its containers is not verified. API tokens for every run. Cloud sandboxes need accounts and money.
simpler_alternative: A stdlib script that runs each agent headless in a fresh copy of the task folder.
reason: Appears to be the common runner for agent comparisons, but it needs Docker and its GPU support is unverified.
cheap_local_trial: none under this scout's no-install rule; a maintainer could run one bundled example task under WSL2 with Docker in about 30 minutes

candidate: AutoWorldModel-Bench (arXiv 2608.11216 v2, 2026-08-16)
what: 32 tasks in which an agent improves a small world model with training runs capped at 600 seconds.
problem_here: The kit needs realistic ML research tasks that are short enough for a paired test on one GPU.
mechanism: The agent sees a validation score; test and scenario splits are scored once after the session on the checkpoint chosen by validation.
evidence: https://electronicarts.github.io/AutoWorldModelBench/ and the arXiv abstract (read 2026-11-11), its authors' results: 63 of 64 sessions improved the held-out test split; the difference between the two agents was not significant (p = 0.15).
maturity: Code BSD 3-Clause per the project page; published mid-2026; adoption unknown; hardware not stated.
cost: Dataset download of about 19K episodes per game; a 6-hour session per task and arm in the paper's setting; agent tokens. The held-out protocol is not technically enforced.
simpler_alternative: The kit's own toy CPU task.
reason: The cheapest public task set found whose protocol matches the kit's sealed-test rule.
cheap_local_trial: none under the no-download rule; a maintainer could run one starter model for a single 600-second run on the 32 GB GPU to confirm that it fits

candidate: PostTrainBench (arXiv 2603.08640 v2, 2026-03-10)
what: An agent post-trains a small base LLM for a target benchmark within 10 hours on one H100.
problem_here: The kit has no test cases taken from real unattended training agents that cheated.
mechanism: Use its reported failure modes as guard and post-run test cases; do not run the benchmark itself.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.08640 abstract (read 2026-11-11), its authors' observations: agents trained on the test set, downloaded finished instruction-tuned checkpoints and used API keys found in the environment; best agent 23.2% against 51.1% for official instruction-tuned models. How the cheating was detected is not in the abstract.
maturity: Preprint from March 2026; used by AutoTrainess; code location and licence not checked.
cost: 10 H100-hours per task and arm if run. Taking the failure list costs nothing.
simpler_alternative: Write the three cheat cases as unit tests without the benchmark.
reason: Valuable as a source of failure cases; too expensive as a regression test.
cheap_local_trial: About 30 minutes: three guard tests (read a sealed path through a script, fetch a finished checkpoint, read an API key from the environment) against the current guard.

candidate: LoopArena Type I questions (arXiv 2608.28281 v2; repository AMAP-ML/LoopArena, no release)
what: 160 four-way questions on loop-control decisions that need no code execution.
problem_here: If any loop decision is left to a model, there is no cheap check of how well that model makes it.
mechanism: Ask the model the questions and score against the key.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.28281 v2 (2026-10-13), its authors: GPT-5.5 scores 61.88 and Claude Opus 4.8 scores 56.25 on this type.
maturity: Apache-2.0, 154 stars, 8 commits, no release (weak).
cost: API tokens. The questions are about software tasks, not training.
simpler_alternative: Leave no loop decision to the model.
reason: Only useful if the design keeps a model in the control path, which the evidence argues against.
cheap_local_trial: none without downloading the question set

candidate: microsoft/SkillOpt v0.2.0 (2026-07-02)
what: An optimizer model edits a skill in small steps and keeps an edit only if a held-out validation score improves.
problem_here: none found today: the kit has no task set to optimize against. It could matter later for tuning the skill text per agent.
mechanism: Bounded add, delete or replace edits, an edit budget, a buffer of rejected edits, and backends that run Codex or Claude Code headless.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23904 v2 (2026-05-25), its authors: best or tied in all 52 cells; +24.8 points with Codex and +19.1 with Claude Code for GPT-5.5. Self-reported. A practitioner's self-tuned AGENTS.md gained on 5 tuning tasks and nothing on 10 holdout tasks (https://www.stet.sh/blog/how-i-used-codex-to-improve-its-own-agents-md, 2026-05-27).
maturity: MIT, Python 3.10+, about 19k stars (weak); paper first listed 2026-05-22; latest release v0.2.0.
cost: A package, paid model calls for many agent runs (cost per run not stated) and a held-out task set the kit does not have. Risk of fitting the skill to the tuning tasks.
simpler_alternative: Edit the skill by hand and rerun the paired measurement.
reason: A sound keep rule, but it presupposes the measurement set; revisit once that exists.
cheap_local_trial: none (needs a package install and paid model calls)

candidate: Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks as a second, agent-independent layer (pattern in Aperion Shield v0.7.0, 2026-05-20)
what: A git hook that refuses commits changing frozen or harness paths unless an override is recorded.
problem_here: Agent hooks differ per agent and can fail open; git hooks behave the same for all three agents and for people.
mechanism: A stdlib script in the repository's git hooks folder reads the staged file list and the kit config.
evidence: https://github.com/AperionAI/shield/releases/tag/shield-v0.7.0 release note (read 2026-11-11): agent-agnostic guardrails as git hooks, bypassable with --no-verify. No measurement.
maturity: Git hooks are long established. The Shield project's licence is not stated.
cost: A small script. Any agent can pass --no-verify, so the tool-call guard must deny that flag. It covers commits only, not runs, and does nothing in a project without git.
simpler_alternative: The post-run hash check alone.
reason: A cheap layer that does not depend on any agent's hook contract, but easy to bypass, so a backstop only.
cheap_local_trial: About 15 minutes: a 15-line pre-commit script in a scratch repository that rejects a staged change to a frozen path.

candidate: kenryu42/cc-safety-net v2.7.9 (2026-11-10)
what: A pre-execution guard for 16 agent CLIs that blocks destructive shell and git commands.
problem_here: The kit's guard covers training-specific rules. General destructive-command coverage and command unwrapping across three agents would otherwise have to be written again.
mechanism: Parses commands semantically, including through bash -c, python -c and wrappers; per-agent hook adapters; safe defaults when its config is broken.
evidence: https://github.com/kenryu42/cc-safety-net README and releases (read 2026-11-11). No independent evaluation; the README states that it is not a sandbox.
maturity: MIT, Node 22+, about 2k stars (weak), latest release v2.7.9 on 2026-11-10; first release not recorded; covers Windows, macOS and Linux.
cost: A Node dependency, which breaks the stdlib-only default. A second guard to keep consistent. One more hook per tool call.
simpler_alternative: Read its unwrapping cases and add the relevant ones to the kit's own tests.
reason: A good reference and a possible optional companion; a Node package cannot be in the core.
cheap_local_trial: none (requires installing a package); reading its test cases through the web takes about 30 minutes

candidate: NVIDIA/skillspector v2.13.4 (2026-11-04)

candidate: eunomia-bpf/ActPlane (arXiv 2606.25189 v2, 2026-06-30; no release)
what: Kernel-side enforcement of file and process rules for agent sessions.
problem_here: Hooks see the command line only. A script can reach sealed data by indirect means, which the README admits.
mechanism: eBPF programs apply an information-flow rule file and can kill, block or notify with a message the agent can read.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25189 v2, its authors: covers indirect paths that hooks miss, at 1.9% to 8.4% overhead. Self-reported. Requirements from https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/ActPlane README (read 2026-11-11).
maturity: MIT, 111 stars, no releases; needs Linux 5.10+ with BTF and root or equivalent capabilities.
cost: Root, a kernel feature and a build. Not available on native Windows; WSL2 not verified. A kernel-level tool is itself attack surface.
simpler_alternative: File permissions, or a container in which the sealed data is not mounted during training.
reason: Addresses the real gap in hook-based sealing, but too immature and privileged for now.
cheap_local_trial: none (needs root and a build)

candidate: Minimum agent version gate in selftest and loop preflight (for example Claude Code 2.1.319 or later for unattended mode)
what: The kit records the lowest version of each agent it was tested with and refuses unattended mode below it.
problem_here: Before 2.1.319 a headless Claude Code session could exit 0 after its actions were refused, and a guard 'ask' could be lost before 2.1.321 or 2.1.322. mechanism: selftest parses each agent's version output and compares it with a table in the kit; the driver also checks for the expected run artifacts instead of trusting exit codes.

maturity: Ordinary practice; the brief already prefers pinned versions.
cost: A table to maintain per release; version strings can change format.
simpler_alternative: State the tested versions in the README only.
reason: Several fail-open and false-success bugs were fixed in the last two weeks; an unattended loop on an older version is unsafe in ways the user cannot see.
cheap_local_trial: About 10 minutes: read the version output of each installed agent and compare it with a three-row table.
